handoff: Blocking F1 (AC4): the tidy summary (tidy.ts:93) and the generated docs/reference.md:406 still describe the removed 'runs/ work not in the record (R2.3)' clean-up and do not mention the superseded prune. Minors: F2, a malformed rejected.json aborts tidy after its removals (dry run included); F3, the no-ref comment at checkout.ts:352 and a silent catch; F4, no --force test for AC1. Nits: F5, F6. Mechanism verified sound.

findings.title: tidy summary and docs/reference.md still name the removed R2.3 clean-up
findings.detail:
The summary reads 'runs/ work not in the record (R2.3)' and docs/reference.md:406 repeats it. tidy no longer does this (the orphaned/ step is gone). It now prunes superseded records after trace.retain, and the summary does not say so. AC4: 'The unpushed_runs fact, its "local work … is not in the record" Check item and the orphaned/ folder are gone: no source … names them'.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Replace that phrase with 'records set aside as superseded (D11)' (older than trace.retain), then run bun run docs:emit.

findings.title: A malformed rejected.json aborts the whole of norn tidy, --dry-run included
findings.detail:
pruneRejectedReceipts calls rejectedForWrite (which throws) even when dry. tidy.ts:182 calls it after worktrees, branches and leases are already removed, so the report of those removals is lost and pruneSuperseded (tidy.ts:184) never runs. A dry run also creates rejected.lock.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: On dry, read without the lock. Otherwise report the refusal in tidy's output (kept/error) and carry on with the other steps.

findings.title: Comment and rule disagree when the holder has no record ref
findings.detail:
With ownRef === null, any remote record counts as newer, so a holder that has not pushed yet sets its live copy aside when someone else pushes a ref. The rule as carried (10-R3-F1: 'or it had no ref and the remote now has one') intends this, and the copy is set aside, not lost. The comment, though, says a ref moved elsewhere is not newer. `.catch(() => false)` on isAncestor is a silent catch.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Make the comment state the no-ref case. Either let the isAncestor failure surface or name why false is safe.

findings.title: AC1's --force takeover is not exercised
findings.detail:
AC1 says 'after expiry (or with --force)'. Every test takes over on expiry. Under remote, a forced take where everything was already pushed reads as on_ref and is removed quietly, with no Check item. Nothing is lost, and the supervisor accepted this per B27's purpose, but it differs from AC1's wording.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Add a --force variant (with a receipt written after the last push) to superseded-record.test.ts. Have the person confirm the remote all-pushed edge, or let slice 18 record it in T7a.

findings.title: Stale comments
findings.detail:
The R2.3 doc comment is left without its removed `unpushed` field. lifecycle.ts:209 says 'observe then reports the local work (R2.3)', which observe no longer does.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Delete or update both comments.

findings.title: Leftover .drop folders are never swept; duplicate inbox ids possible
findings.detail:
A crash between rename and rm leaves .<story>.drop-* or .<name>.drop folders that nothing lists or removes. items.ts:791 gives the id superseded:<story>:<last_receipt>, so two copies of one story with the same last receipt collide. superseded.ts:142 uses a cast as a null sentinel.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Have tidy sweep the dot-drop folders. Use the copy's name in the item id.
